scope: Production retained compiler workers: changing application edits with six bundled-library imports. Browser memoryOnly sessions accept one source and lazily check bundled modules; they cannot load arbitrary project files. This is not a multi-file incremental-project benchmark, UI responsiveness budget, physical mobile test, or network-delivery measurement.
timing: Page performance.now immediately before worker.postMessage until the matching response: includes structured clone, queue, raw-source guest bridge, compiler execution, and response. Worker boot excluded from edit timing. Fresh first check includes lazy imported-module checking; warm check and compile reuse the same worker/environment. Hover follows each changed check and is timed separately.
hostConditions: Shared Apple M5 Pro host running unrelated compiler builds and tests in other worktrees; no parent-task browser/build work during measurements. Results are diagnostic, not an idle-host acceptance budget.

fixture.source:
local json = require("nupp.codec.json")
local hex = require("nupp.codec.hex")
local text = require("nupp.text")
local utf8 = require("nupp.text.utf8")
local path = require("nupp.io.path")
local uri = require("nupp.io.uri")

local type Player = {
    name: string,
    score: integer,
    connected: boolean
}
local type Snapshot = {
    round: integer,
    names: {string},
    total: integer,
    payload: string
}

local function scorePlayers(players: {Player}, round: integer): Snapshot
    local names: {string} = {}
    local total: integer = 0
    for _, player in ipairs(players) do
        if player.connected then
            names[#names + 1] = utf8.truncate(player.name, 24)
            total = total + player.score
        end
    end
    table.sort(names)
    local payload = json.encode({round = round, players = names, total = total})

    return {round = round, names = names, total = total, payload = payload}
end

local function describe(snapshot: Snapshot): string
    local out = text.newBuffer()
    out:put("round=", tostring(snapshot.round), "\n")
    out:put("players=", table.concat(snapshot.names, ", "), "\n")
    out:put("total=", tostring(snapshot.total), "\n")
    out:put("payload=", hex.encode(snapshot.payload), "\n")

    return out:get()
end

local function destination(round: integer): (string, string)
    local localFile = path.newPath("scores", "round-" .. tostring(round)):withExtension("json")
    local endpoint = assert(uri.newURI("https://game.example/scores/"))
    local remoteFile = assert(endpoint:resolve(assert(localFile:fileName())))
    return localFile:toString(), remoteFile:toString()
end

local players: {
    Player
} = {
    {name = "Ada", score = 120, connected = true},
    {name = "Lin", score = 90, connected = true},
    {name = "Grace", score = 140, connected = false},
}
local round: integer = 5
local snapshot = scorePlayers(players, round)
local localFile, remoteFile = destination(round)
local report = describe(snapshot)
local wire = hex.encode("scoreboard-edit-5")
assert(hex.decode(wire) == "scoreboard-edit-5")
assert(snapshot.total == 210)
assert(utf8.length(snapshot.names[1]) == 3)
return report, localFile, remoteFile, wire

edits: Replace round integer 5 and both scoreboard-edit-5 string literals with trial+5 on every request. Each compile must contain its current changed string. Every check/compile must return zero errors; every hover must identify wire as string. After timing, each imported API must reject a wrong argument with NUPP2006.

responseEquivalence: All 18 successful backend sessions have identical hover types and complete imported-argument diagnostics within each engine. All changed valid checks/compiles passed, and emitted code retained each current edited string.
harnessCaveat: Initial WebKit attempt with Playwright network interception timed out at boot. The diagnostic rerun confirms boot timeout, before requests. Removing interception alone restores successful boots, matching the known Playwright WebKit blob-worker limitation documented in browser-matrix.mjs. Final WebKit sessions use real HTTP navigation. Chromium/Firefox sessions use the initial empty-page route; request timing begins after boot and both backends within each engine use the same route. Raw failed/pilot attempts are preserved in imported-harness-probe.json and excluded from timing summaries.
